andhraPradesh.headline: Veligonda Project Phase I inaugurated; Krishna water released into Nallamala Sagar
facts: The first phase of the Poola Subbaiah Veligonda irrigation project was inaugurated and water was released into Nallamala Sagar on 31 August.
Phase I was reported completed at a cost of ₹7,983 crore, against a total estimated project cost of ₹10,200 crore.
The completed first-phase works include twin tunnels of 18.8 km and feeder canals of 21.8 km.
The phase is designed to store 10.70 TMC of Krishna water, irrigate 1.19 lakh acres and provide drinking water to about four lakh people.
The government stated that Phase II is to be completed by 2028; this remains a future target.
andhraPradesh.summary: The inauguration and water release mark a major irrigation milestone for drought-prone Markapuram and adjoining areas. Phase I is inaugurated and completed, but the full project is not; Phase II remains planned for completion by 2028.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Major irrigation projects, inter-basin water transfer, drought mitigation and regional development in Andhra Pradesh.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Veligonda transfers Krishna water from the Srisailam reservoir towards Nallamala Sagar; distinguish the completed Phase I from the still-pending Phase II.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how irrigation infrastructure can address drought and drinking-water needs while requiring rehabilitation of displaced families and long-term project completion.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The project is in Andhra Pradesh and is intended to benefit Markapuram and surrounding drought-prone areas.

- **Water transfer:** From **Srisailam reservoir** towards **Nallamala Sagar**

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh’s monsoon deficit reached about 45% by the end of August, affecting kharif sowing
facts: For 1 June–31 August, Andhra Pradesh received 204.3 mm of rain against a normal of 369.5 mm, a deficit of about 45%.
The reported 2026 kharif sown area was 20.35 lakh hectares, compared with 25.63 lakh hectares at the corresponding point in 2025.
All 28 districts were reported rainfall-deficient; Annamayya, Prakasam and Bapatla were classified as severely deficient.
Annamayya had the highest reported deficit at 69%; Bapatla and Prakasam each recorded 59%.
The article attributed the poor rainfall largely to El Niño conditions; the reported figures describe rainfall through 31 August, not a forecast.
andhraPradesh.summary: A severe rainfall shortfall through August coincided with a lower kharif sown area in Andhra Pradesh than at the same point the previous year. The district-level variation and reduced sowing make the situation relevant to crop planning, water management and farmer support.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Indian monsoon, rainfall variability, kharif agriculture and drought management.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Reported AP rainfall deficit to 31 August 2026: about 45%; reported kharif sowing: 20.35 lakh hectares, against 25.63 lakh hectares in the corresponding period of 2025.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how rainfall variability affects agricultural output and rural livelihoods, and evaluate the roles of contingency crop planning, irrigation and timely relief.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The reported rainfall and sowing figures concern Andhra Pradesh and identify district-level impacts, including in Annamayya, Bapatla and Prakasam.

andhraPradesh.headline: Godavari water release through Polavaram Left Main Canal scheduled for 2 September
facts: On 1 September, the state announced that Godavari water would be released through the Polavaram Project Left Main Canal on 2 September at Payakaraopeta in Anakapalli district.
The reported canal construction expenditure was ₹4,192 crore; the canal is about 213 km long.
The initial planned benefit is irrigation across 2.87 lakh acres in four districts and drinking-water supply for 5.23 lakh people.
In Anakapalli district, about 1.5 lakh acres are expected to benefit; water is also planned to fill the Yeleru canal and 110 tanks.
The canal is planned for eventual integration with the North Andhra Sujala Sravanthi project; the 1 September report described the release as scheduled, not completed.
andhraPradesh.summary: The state announced a scheduled release of Godavari water into the Polavaram Left Main Canal for 2 September. The proposed distribution network is intended to support irrigation and drinking-water needs in North Andhra, with Anakapalli among the immediate beneficiaries.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Polavaram Project, canal irrigation, river-basin transfer and regional water management.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: On 1 September, the release through the Polavaram Left Main Canal was announced for the following day; its initial planned coverage was 2.87 lakh acres and 5.23 lakh people.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine the role of canal networks and inter-basin transfers in regional water security, alongside the need for accurate command-area planning and sustainable allocation.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The canal and announced release directly concern Anakapalli and the wider North Andhra region of Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: ₹100 crore sanctioned for Godavari-basin infrastructure ahead of Pushkaralu
facts: The Deputy Chief Minister sanctioned ₹100 crore through the Panchayat Raj and Rural Water Supply department for works across seven constituencies in three districts.
The allocation is under the theme “Swachh Godavari – Pavitra Pushkaralu” and is additional to a separately reported ₹100 crore allocation through the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board.
Of the new sanction, ₹90 crore is for 111 projects, including about 141 km of cement-concrete and bituminous roads.
The remaining ₹10 crore is intended for safe drinking-water facilities for pilgrims.
The reported road routes connect villages with ghats in Razole, P. Gannavaram, Ramachandrapuram, Rampachodavaram, Achanta, Narsapuram and Palakollu constituencies.
andhraPradesh.summary: The state sanctioned ₹100 crore for village connectivity and drinking-water works ahead of the Godavari Pushkaralu. The report describes a sanction and planned works; it does not establish that the projects have been completed.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Local-government service delivery, rural infrastructure, sanitation and pilgrimage management.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The reported ₹100-crore Panchayat Raj/RWS sanction includes ₹90 crore for 111 works and ₹10 crore for drinking water.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Evaluate how event-linked public investment can improve durable rural infrastructure, and identify the importance of transparent project selection and maintenance.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The works cover Godavari-basin constituencies and districts in Andhra Pradesh, including areas around the named pilgrimage ghats.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh training institutes oriented on Mission Karmayogi’s UNNATI Portal
facts: The Capacity Building Commission held a virtual orientation and onboarding session on 1 September for more than 35 Andhra Pradesh state training institutes.
UNNATI expands to Unified New-Age National Training Initiative and is a portal under Mission Karmayogi.
The session covered registration and onboarding, resource-sharing and use of the portal by training institutes.
The Commission described the institutes’ role as translating Capacity Building Plans into training for government personnel.
The session urged institutes to complete registration; the report does not state that all institutes had completed onboarding.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Capacity Building Commission conducted an orientation for Andhra Pradesh training institutes on using the UNNATI Portal. The session focused on onboarding and collaborative capacity-building; participation in the orientation should not be read as completed registration by every institute.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Civil-service capacity building, Mission Karmayogi and digital governance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: UNNATI means Unified New-Age National Training Initiative and is linked to Mission Karmayogi.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how shared digital platforms and coordinated training can strengthen state administrative capacity, while noting the importance of actual adoption and measurable outcomes.
andhraPradesh.apLink: More than 35 Andhra Pradesh state training institutes took part in the orientation, including state-level capacity-building institutions.

- ⚠ **Trap:** Participation in the orientation does not mean that every institute had completed registration or onboarding.
> Exam angle: Expand **UNNATI** and connect the portal with **Mission Karmayogi** and training-institute capacity building.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh High Court directs EPFO to decide retired workers’ higher-pension representation
facts: In Venum Surya Narayana v. Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, W.P. No. 21456 of 2026, the Andhra Pradesh High Court issued its order on 1 September.
The petitioners, former workers associated with the Dowleswaram facility in East Godavari, sought correction of provident-fund records and consideration of their joint option for higher pension.
The Court directed the respondents to examine the petitioners’ representation dated 19 March 2026 and communicate a decision within three months.
The order disposed of the writ petition; it did not itself grant higher pension or decide the representation’s merits.
andhraPradesh.summary: The High Court directed the EPFO authorities to consider and decide retired workers’ representation concerning provident-fund records and the higher-pension option within three months. The order requires administrative consideration rather than granting the pension claim itself.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Judicial review under Article 226, administrative accountability and social-security entitlements.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The Court disposed of the writ petition with a direction to decide the representation within three months; it did not determine the pension claim on its merits.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Consider how judicial review can secure timely administrative decisions in social-security matters without substituting the court’s decision for the competent authority’s merits review.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The petitioners were former workers associated with Dowleswaram in East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh.

- **Order date:** **1 September 2026**
- **Petitioners:** Former workers associated with the **Dowleswaram facility**, **East Godavari district**
- **Relief sought:** Correction of provident-fund records and consideration of their joint option for higher pension

> Exam angle: Distinguish a direction to decide an administrative representation from a judgment granting higher pension.

national.headline: India’s real GDP grows 7.8% in Q1 FY 2026–27
facts: MoSPI released the Q1 GDP estimates on 31 August 2026; the quarter covers April–June 2026.
Real GDP was estimated at ₹81.36 lakh crore, up 7.8% year-on-year; growth was 6.9% in Q1 FY 2025–26.
Nominal GDP was estimated at ₹88.27 lakh crore, a 10.3% increase.
Real GVA grew 8.2%; investment grew 11.9%, household consumption 7.1%, and exports 12.0%.
The PIB backgrounder attributed growth support to manufacturing, services and domestic demand; no AP-specific figure was established in the cited release.
national.summary: MoSPI’s Q1 FY 2026–27 estimates showed real GDP growth of 7.8%, compared with 6.9% in the year-earlier quarter. The figures are relevant for assessing growth composition, domestic demand and the distinction between real and nominal GDP.
national.staticLink: National income accounting; GDP, GVA, real and nominal growth; expenditure components of GDP.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Q1 FY 2026–27 real GDP growth: 7.8%; nominal GDP growth: 10.3%; real GVA growth: 8.2%.
national.mainsAngle: Assess the drivers and sustainability of growth, including the balance between consumption, investment, exports and sectoral performance.

national.headline: ZSI reports new deep-sea skate species from the southeastern Arabian Sea
facts: The Zoological Survey of India, ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute and international experts described a new skate species, Dipturus dhritiae, also called the Arabian Skate.
The species was reported from deep-water habitats off Kerala and the Wadge Bank region in the southeastern Arabian Sea.
Specimens were collected at depths of 400–600 metres; the reported maximum known length is 131.5 cm.
The discovery arose from exploratory work under the Ministry of Earth Sciences’ Deep Ocean Mission project on Indian chondrichthyans.
The research team mapped the Kollam Slope Important Shark and Ray Area within India’s Exclusive Economic Zone.
national.summary: A ZSI-led team described Dipturus dhritiae, a new deep-sea skate species found off Kerala and the Wadge Bank region. The report connects marine taxonomy with deep-sea biodiversity research and the need to monitor vulnerable habitats.
national.staticLink: India’s Exclusive Economic Zone; marine biodiversity; Deep Ocean Mission; taxonomy and conservation of chondrichthyans.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Dipturus dhritiae was reported from 400–600 metre depths off Kerala and the Wadge Bank region; the discovery was linked to the Deep Ocean Mission.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how deep-sea exploration can advance biodiversity knowledge while strengthening evidence-based protection of marine habitats.
national.apLink: The species was reported off Kerala, not Andhra Pradesh; no direct AP-specific link established.

sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

- **Described by:** **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**, **ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute** and international experts
- **Status:** **COMPLETED**; new species described
# 2. Location and features
| Basis | Finding |
|---|---|
| Region | Deep-water habitats off **Kerala** and the **Wadge Bank** region, southeastern **Arabian Sea** |
| Collection depth | **400–600 metres** |
| Maximum known length | **131.5 cm** |
| Mapped area | **Kollam Slope Important Shark and Ray Area**, within India’s **Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)** |

- **Andhra Pradesh link:** No direct AP-specific link established; the species was reported off **Kerala**, not **Andhra Pradesh**

> Exam angle: Identify the new marine species, its reported region and its link to the Deep Ocean Mission.

national.headline: Defence production reaches about ₹1.8 lakh crore in FY 2025–26, says Defence Ministry
facts: The Defence Minister reviewed the annual performance of 16 Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) in New Delhi on 1 September 2026.
The Ministry reported defence production of approximately ₹1.8 lakh crore in FY 2025–26.
DPSUs contributed approximately ₹1.29 lakh crore of that production value.

national.summary: The annual review highlighted reported FY 2025–26 defence production of about ₹1.8 lakh crore, with DPSUs accounting for about ₹1.29 lakh crore. The government also emphasized timely delivery, exports, research and development, and reduced import dependence.

national.headline: Air Vice Marshal Shakti Sharma becomes first non-medical woman officer to attain the rank
facts: Air Vice Marshal Shakti Sharma became the first woman officer in the Indian Defence Forces, outside the medical stream, to attain the rank of Air Vice Marshal or equivalent, according to the Ministry of Defence.
On 1 September 2026, she assumed the appointment of Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (Education) at Air Headquarters.
She was commissioned into the Indian Air Force Education Branch on 18 June 1994.
The Ministry also reported that she was the first woman officer from the three services to command a Sainik School; she served as Principal of Sainik School, Kapurthala.
national.summary: Shakti Sharma assumed the Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (Education) appointment and attained the rank of Air Vice Marshal. The Ministry of Defence identified her as the first non-medical woman officer in India’s defence forces to reach that rank.
national.staticLink: Women’s representation in the armed forces; gender equality; institutional leadership and public service.
national.prelimsTakeaway: AVM Shakti Sharma: first non-medical woman officer in India’s defence forces to attain Air Vice Marshal rank; assumed ACAS (Education) on 1 September 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Use the appointment to discuss representation, institutional pathways and the role of equal opportunity in strengthening public institutions.

national.headline: Government announces lower sugar stock limit for most dealers from 15 September
facts: On 1 September 2026, the Government announced a reduction in the sugar stock limit for dealers from 4,000 to 2,000 quintals.
The revised limit was announced to apply from 15 September through 30 November 2026; it was not yet in force on the announcement date.
Dealers may not hold stock for more than 30 days from receipt, under the announced provisions.
Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas retain a 4,000-quintal limit, according to the release.
The stated objectives are to curb hoarding and speculative trading and support domestic availability and price stability.
national.summary: The government announced tighter, time-limited sugar stock controls, with the general dealer limit scheduled to fall to 2,000 quintals from 15 September 2026. The Kolkata metropolitan exception was retained at 4,000 quintals; the announcement date and effective date are distinct.
national.staticLink: Essential commodities; food supply management; market regulation; price stability.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Announced dealer limit: 2,000 quintals from 15 September to 30 November 2026; Kolkata metropolitan area: 4,000 quintals.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the use of stock limits to prevent hoarding and stabilize essential-goods supply, alongside the need for transparent, proportionate market regulation.

national.headline: Railways approves ₹170 crore for Kavach 4.0 on 712 route-km in Moradabad Division
facts: Indian Railways approved ₹170 crore for Kavach Version 4.0 on the remaining sections covering 712 route-kilometres in Moradabad Division, Northern Railway.
Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system.
The system is designed to help prevent Signal Passing at Danger, control train speed in critical conditions and apply brakes when required.
The approved work is a planned deployment; the approval does not mean the system is already operational across the sections.
national.summary: Indian Railways approved funding to extend Kavach 4.0 across 712 route-kilometres in Moradabad Division. The release describes the system’s safety functions, while the approved deployment remains a project to be implemented.
national.staticLink: Railway safety; indigenous technology; automatic train protection; public infrastructure.

national.mainsAngle: Examine how indigenous safety technology can reduce operational risk, and why implementation, testing and maintenance matter alongside project approval.

national.headline: CAQM reviews NCR inspections and compliance measures at its 138th Enforcement Task Force meeting
facts: The Commission for Air Quality Management’s 138th Enforcement Task Force meeting was held on 31 August 2026; PIB reported the review on 1 September.
For the 16-day reporting period from 8 to 23 August, flying squads conducted 121 inspections across NCR.
The inspections included 56 in the industrial sector, 20 relating to diesel generator sets and 10 at construction and demolition sites.
Proposals based on reported violations included closure of four projects or industries, sealing 17 diesel generator sets, seven compliance directions and environmental compensation in five cases.
By 31 August, flying squads had conducted 28,397 cumulative inspections across NCR; 1,823 closure directions and 1,473 resumption orders had been recorded.
national.summary: CAQM reviewed enforcement activity and compliance across the National Capital Region, reporting inspections and proposed actions based on violations. The meeting date was 31 August; the PIB update was published the following day.
national.staticLink: Air pollution governance; environmental compliance; statutory commissions and enforcement.
national.prelimsTakeaway: CAQM is the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas; its Enforcement Task Force reviewed 121 inspections for 8–23 August 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Assess the importance of inspection capacity, compliance verification and coordination among agencies in translating air-quality rules into enforceable outcomes.

international.headline: 26th SCO Summit adopts Bishkek Declaration and cooperation outcomes
facts: The 26th SCO Council of Heads of State met in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, during 31 August–1 September 2026; the summit marked the organisation’s 25th anniversary.
India participated through Prime Minister Narendra Modi; Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov chaired the summit.
Leaders adopted the Bishkek Declaration and more than 20 decisions and statements, including outcomes on climate, nuclear safety, energy conservation and combating drug addiction.
India-backed initiatives included use of English as an official language in the SCO Charter, a Civilisation Dialogue Forum, a Young Scientist Forum and a Young Authors’ Conclave.

The declaration addressed multilateral cooperation including security, trade, climate, public health, science and technology; it welcomed India’s hosting of the SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum in autumn 2026.
international.summary: The 26th SCO summit concluded in Bishkek with the anniversary declaration and a range of cooperation outcomes. India participated and advanced initiatives on language, civilisational dialogue and youth engagement; the SCO’s stated positions are political commitments and cooperation priorities, not proof that each proposed activity has already been implemented.
international.staticLink: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation; regional multilateralism; India’s engagement with Central Asia; international cooperation on security and sustainable development.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the 26th Council of Heads of State meeting, Bishkek as host, the organisation’s 25th anniversary, and the Bishkek Declaration. Distinguish adopted declarations and decisions from measures already implemented.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how India can use regional forums such as the SCO to advance security, connectivity and development while navigating differing member-state interests.

international.headline: India and Germany sign wetlands conservation declaration at environment forum
facts: The 4th Indo-German Environment Forum was held in New Delhi on 1 September under the theme “Together For More Resilience.”
The forum was co-chaired by India’s Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Germany’s Federal Environment Minister Carsten Schneider.
The ministers signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on the conservation and wise use of wetlands of international importance.
Forum discussions covered low-carbon industries, biodiversity in wetlands, mountains and forests, circular economy, sustainable finance and green skills.
The forum is the highest-level bilateral platform between India and Germany on environmental policy and has been held since 2008.
international.summary: India and Germany used the 4th Indo-German Environment Forum to deepen environmental cooperation and signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on wetlands. The declaration sets out cooperation on conservation and wise use; it should not be described as a completed wetland project or as a treaty.
international.staticLink: Ramsar Convention and wetland conservation; India’s environmental diplomacy; bilateral environmental cooperation.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The forum’s theme was “Together For More Resilience,” and its wetlands outcome was a Joint Declaration of Intent. Distinguish an intent declaration from a binding treaty or a completed conservation project.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how bilateral environmental partnerships can support wetland conservation, biodiversity protection and climate resilience, while noting the need for implementation and local participation.

international.headline: BHASHINI SANGAM workshop advances India–Nepal collaboration on multilingual AI
facts: The Digital India BHASHINI Division organised BHASHINI SANGAM: International Engagement Workshop (Nepal) in Kathmandu, in collaboration with the Embassy of India and Kathmandu University.
The workshop built on an existing memorandum of understanding between BHASHINI and Kathmandu University on language technology and digital public infrastructure.
Participants explored co-creating technology, datasets and locally relevant Language AI applications for communities in India and Nepal.

Demonstrations covered speech recognition, real-time translation, voice-enabled interaction and document processing; the workshop also included a BhashaDaan session on community-contributed language data.
The Government of India describes BHASHINI as its national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion.
international.summary: The Kathmandu workshop advanced an existing India–Nepal partnership on language technology through demonstrations and discussion of locally relevant applications. The reported development was a collaboration workshop; the source does not say that the proposed applications were launched or deployed.
international.staticLink: Digital public infrastructure; artificial intelligence and language technology; inclusive access to public services; India–Nepal relations.
international.prelimsTakeaway: BHASHINI is associated with AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. The Kathmandu engagement built on an existing MoU with Kathmandu University; the workshop itself did not establish that new applications had been launched.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how multilingual AI and cross-border academic collaboration can widen access to digital public services, while addressing language-data representation and community participation.
